analysis: Changed file is only a CI regression test (.github/scripts/test-threat-model-review.py). The hunk at head lines 743 and 752-761 changes the workflow-boundary assertions in WorkflowBoundaryTests.test_secret_bearing_workflow_separates_current_scanner_from_pinned_base_context. THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA is now asserted to come only from github.event.pull_request.base.sha, with no env fallback, which is stricter. The timeout is asserted at 60 minutes with THREAT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 3000. The test also asserts the Bedrock call policy is workload with bounded call and token variables, and that the review job has no workflow_dispatch, pr_number or review_depth input. These removals of manual-dispatch inputs reduce the risk of attacker-selected PR/base context in the secret-bearing workflow. The test only inspects the workflow text and does not change runtime behavior. The changes touch none of the provider, coordinator, attestation, key, cache or fan-helper assets, so the threat-model entries in scope (T-041 etc.) are not affected. The workflow YAML (.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml) and the scanner modules were not supplied. I cannot confirm that the workflow actually matches these assertions, and that is the one open integration question. If a workflow change ships in the same PR, it needs its own review for the secret-bearing pull_request_target boundary and for cost and availability bounds (the 500-call cap, the 60-minute timeout). No concrete security regression is visible in the supplied evidence.
